title: OpenCode HTTP Session Cleanup Tool
summary: The FP-MCP-253 explicit OpenCode HTTP session cleanup tool was implemented, exposed, and verified against the intentionally retained FP-MCP-251 canary session. The tool deleted exactly session ses_0d5e10bf0fferWGbj7B9Hk8Ec8 after requiring sessionId and confirmSessionId to match and requiring approval DELETE_OPENCODE_HTTP_SESSION. The deletion returned deleteRan=true, explicitSessionIdMatched=true, sessionDeleted=true, deleteHttpStatus=200, deleteContentType=application/json, and authConfigured=true. The tool also confirmed sessionCreated=false, promptSubmitted=false, messageEndpointCalled=false, waitEndpointCalled=false, runnerStartEndpointContacted=false, and opencodeStarted=false. This closes the intentional leftover session caveat from FP-MCP-251 and establishes an explicit, guarded cleanup mechanism for future HTTP lifecycle tools.
caveats: The cleanup tool is intentionally destructive for the explicitly named session, so it requires duplicate session-id confirmation plus a fixed approval literal.
The tool does not verify post-delete absence via a follow-up read; it records the DELETE /session/{id} HTTP result only.
The cleanup target was the intentionally retained canary session from FP-MCP-251, not an arbitrary or discovered session.
boundaries: No OpenCode session was created by the cleanup tool.
No prompt was submitted by the cleanup tool.
No message endpoint was read by the cleanup tool.
No wait endpoint was called by the cleanup tool.
No OpenCode process was started by the cleanup tool.
No ForgePilot runner start endpoint was contacted by the cleanup tool.
No execution approval was created, consumed, or authorized by the cleanup tool.
Only the explicitly named session id was targeted.
